To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
there are many definitions and models of data provenance, but they are often limited in their scope.

the different provenance models can be categorized into five classes, namely: data-centric, process-centric, data-centric and process-centric, process-centric and data-centric, and data-centric and processcentric provenance models.
the existing approaches are limited to a certain application domain and data model and that the existing approaches do not provide a general solution to provenance problems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a comprehensive provenance model, which is able to capture the different kinds of information required in different application domains.
the following questions: Which kinds of provenance are relevant for a given application?
the question how to represent provenance information in a generic and application independent manner.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
data provenance has not yet reached its maturity.
there is no single best solution for data provenance.
there is no such thing as provenance in general but a variety of different kinds of provenances.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the current research in the area of provenance is still in a rather preliminary stage and that there are many open problems to solve.
the provenance research community has made a good start but still has a long way to go.
there is no single provenance approach that is suitable for all kinds of data representation models, data processing facilities or application areas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the existing approaches to data provenance are not sufficient for many application scenarios.
we can distinguish between different kinds and levels of data provenance and that these different levels of provenance information require different storage, transformation and querying techniques.

there is no single best provenance approach for all application domains and data representation models, but that there are a number of different approaches, each of them tailored for a specific application domain and data representation model.
